intro: Level B2: from describing a situation to an argued position. This week the topic of work is explored through remote work, burnout, motivation and salary negotiations.
speaking.0.promptUa: Describe the illustration and comment on the situation. Say what you think are the advantages and disadvantages of remote work and whether you would like to work that way.
speaking.0.phrases.0.ua: In the foreground you can see… / in the background…
speaking.0.phrases.1.ua: It seems that… / One can assume that…
speaking.0.phrases.2.ua: On the one hand… on the other hand…
speaking.0.phrases.3.ua: In my opinion the best solution is…
speaking.0.tips.0: At B2 the examiner expects **description + interpretation + your own opinion**. Don't stop at «widzę kobietę» — go on to «wydaje się, że…».
speaking.0.tips.1: The structure «**z jednej strony… z drugiej strony…**» immediately improves the impression of coherence.
speaking.0.tips.2: Finish with a personal position: the examiner assesses your ability to argue, not just to describe.
speaking.1.promptUa: State your position on the claim: «It is better to have a well-paid job that you don't enjoy than a job that gives satisfaction but pays little». Justify it, give examples and take another point of view into account.
speaking.1.phrases.0.ua: I don't agree with this claim because…
speaking.1.phrases.2.ua: Of course I understand the argument that…, however…
speaking.1.phrases.3.ua: To sum up, one can say that…
speaking.1.tips.0: Always **mention the counter-argument** («Oczywiście rozumiem…, jednak…») — it is a direct point of the «argumentacja» criterion.
speaking.1.tips.1: An example from life («znam to z doświadczenia…») makes the answer convincing and gives you time to think.
speaking.1.tips.2: Aim for 2–3 minutes: 3 ideas of 40 seconds each + a conclusion.
speaking.2.promptUa: You are talking to your manager. You want a pay rise. Present your arguments, respond to her reservations and try to reach a compromise.
speaking.2.phrases.0.ua: I would like to talk about my salary.
writing.0.promptUa: You are a project manager. You need to change the date of Thursday's team meeting because the client moved the presentation. Write an e-mail to the team: the reason, the new date and place, a request to confirm attendance and to prepare short reports.
writing.0.phrases.0.ua: Because of the change of date… we have to postpone…
writing.0.phrases.2.ua: At the same time I ask you to prepare…
writing.0.phrases.3.ua: If you have any difficulties, please get in touch.
writing.0.tips.0: In a short business e-mail **each sentence carries one point** — and no unnecessary preamble.
writing.0.tips.1: A polite form of request: **«Proszę o + accusative/genitive»** (proszę o potwierdzenie) — businesslike and compact.
writing.1.promptUa: Your company is considering permanent remote work. Write an article for the company blog with your position: list the pros and cons, refer to your own experience and propose a solution.
writing.1.phrases.1.ua: In my opinion… / I believe that…
writing.1.phrases.2.ua: However, we must not forget that…
writing.1.tips.0: The scheme **thesis → arguments «for» → arguments «against» → own experience → proposal → conclusion** works for any argumentative text.
writing.1.tips.1: The conditional («pozwoliłyby», «dałyby») is an example of «zakres środków» that a B2 examiner looks for.
writing.1.tips.2: Use **dzięki czemu / co prowadzi do** — that's how you build complex sentences with cause and effect.
listening.0.intro: Listen to the radio interview extract and choose the correct answers.
grammar.0.intro: B2: complex sentences, the passive, participles. Choose the form that fits grammatically.
grammar.0.questions.3.why: Present adverbial participle (**-ąc**): «Decydując się na… warto…» — two actions by the same subject.
vocab.7.ua: to settle into a job, to find one's feet
